name: OPA209 / OPA2209 / OPA4209 (TI 36 V, 2.2 nV/rtHz bipolar, rail-to-rail output)
tagline: A low-power 36 V TI precision op-amp (2.2 nV/rtHz, 2.5 mA/ch max, rail-to-rail output) that Head-Fi op-amp rollers praise for detail and treble clarity.
technology: Bipolar-input precision op-amp. Supply 4.5 V to 36 V (±2.25 V to ±18 V). 2.2 nV/rtHz at 1 kHz, 18 MHz GBW, 6.4 V/us slew rate, rail-to-rail output, 2.5 mA per channel max quiescent current, 150 uV max offset. SMD packages only: SOT-23-5, MSOP-8, SOIC-8, TSSOP-14.

part_numbers.status: active (TI product page is live; status not explicitly confirmed in this pass)
part_numbers.notes: Single. Orderable examples: OPA209AIDBVT (SOT-23-5) and OPA209AIDR (SOIC-8). MSOP-8 is probably also offered (unconfirmed).
Dual. Orderable example: OPA2209AID (SOIC-8). MSOP-8 is also listed for the family. TI marks the device ACTIVE.

key_specs.condition: 25 C. The 35 uV typical value comes only from a mirror's file name ('35uV Vos') and is unconfirmed.

reputation.summary: Several op-amp rollers name it a favourite in Head-Fi's 'The Opamp thread' and in the xDuoo XD-05 op-amp rolling threads. One poster calls it their 'favorite bipolar' and credits it with 'amazing resolution and detail level', 'great soundstage depth', an airy sound and 'the best treble detail and clarity'. Other posters rank it with the OPA2189 and OPA1692 among the top three duals on specs. Some comparisons are more mixed: one found it 'somewhat laid back' like the OP275, and another found its background brighter or noisier than the OPA1692's. These are individual forum impressions and were not re-checked in this pass.
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in the xDuoo XD-05 portable DAC/amp and similar socketed gear (needs an SMD-to-DIP adapter)
DAC output / filter stages (TI lists high-performance DAC output amplifiers as an application)
caveats: The praise is subjective and comes from a handful of Head-Fi posters.
One comparison heard a brighter or noisier background than the OPA1692.
It is a precision general-purpose part, not a TI SoundPlus audio part.
It is sold in SMD packages only, so DIP-8 sockets need an adapter board.

counterfeit_notes: No specific counterfeit reports were found in this pass. TI makes the family only in SMD packages (SOT-23-5, MSOP-8, SOIC-8, TSSOP-14). Any 'DIP-8 OPA2209' must therefore be an SMD die on an adapter board, or a fake. Check the top marking and buy from authorised distributors.
alternatives: OPA2210 (TI, 2.2 nV/rtHz 36 V precision bipolar, newer)
open_questions: Is there an SBOS426 revision later than D (October 2016)? None was found by search.
Date and content of SBOS426A, and what changed in revs B, C and D (for example, when the OPA2209 and OPA4209 were added).
Which SBOS426 revision each mirror holds: Mouser 556484, Octopart 10674197 and 21095356, UToronto, RadioLocman, Alldatasheet.
No OPA209-specific PCN (die revision or fab transfer) was found. Generic TI RFAB/FFAB PCNs appeared in search but were not tied to this family.
Unconfirmed specs to add from the datasheet: 0.1-10 Hz noise, offset drift, input bias current, THD+N and the exact per-part package list.
